item.title: 2A alert: 9th Cir. en banc reverses Hawaii gun-permit win (Yukutake v. Lopez) — upholds 30-day buy window + inspection under Bruen n.9
item.description:
2A alert (~1:46 PM ET Tue Sep 22):

Yukutake v. Lopez — Ninth Circuit en banc reverses Hawaii firearm-permit injunction.

What is new:
• U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, en banc, No. 21-16756, opinion filed Sep. 22, 2026.
• Caption: Todd Yukutake; David Kikukawa v. Anne E. Lopez (Hawaii AG); City & County of Honolulu also a defendant. D. Haw. No. 1:19-cv-00578-JMS-RT.
• Opinion by Judge Owens; dissents by Judge R. Nelson (joined in part), Judge Forrest, and Judge VanDyke. Vacates prior three-judge panel affirmance.
• Disposition: REVERSED AND REMANDED.

Holding:
Court holds Hawaii’s shall-issue regime comports with the Second Amendment. Challenged provisions — Haw. Rev. Stat. § 134-2(e) (handgun acquisition permit void unless used within 30 days) and § 134-3 (registration form + bring firearm to police for inspection in certain circumstances) — are treated as presumptively lawful under Bruen footnote 9. Plaintiffs failed to show the provisions were put toward “abusive ends” that would effectively deny ordinary citizens their Second Amendment rights; at most “modest, procedural burdens.”

Why it matters:
En banc reversal after a district-court permanent injunction and a prior panel affirmance for the plaintiffs. Entrenches Bruen n.9 as a practical safe harbor for objective shall-issue conditions in the Ninth Circuit. Dissents argue the majority misreads footnote 9 and that the government still must prove history and tradition.

Caveats:
• Not a ruling on may-issue; majority notes lengthy waits, high fees, etc. could still trigger Second Amendment scrutiny.
• Disposition is reverse and remand; no stay language in the ordered line.
• Forrest dissent also addresses statewide injunction breadth.

Primary source:
https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2026/09/22/21-16756.pdf

item.title: 2A breaking: 5th Cir. strikes federal interstate handgun purchase ban; Cordova en banc set Jan 2027
item.description:
2A Watch — material update (Mon Sep 21, 2026 ~6:40 PM ET)
Verified / factual only — not advocacy.

1) Fifth Circuit — Elite Precision Customs v. ATF, No. 25-11206
Filed: Sep 18, 2026 (missed by earlier Sep 18–21 watches).
Panel: Smith, J. (majority); Haynes, J., dissenting; Engelhardt, J., on panel.
Holding: The federal Nonresident Handgun Purchase Ban — 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(a)(3), (a)(5), and (b)(3), taken together — violates the Second Amendment under Bruen. Court reversed the N.D. Tex. dismissal and rendered judgment for plaintiffs. Treated the scheme as a categorical direct-purchase ban (FFL-to-FFL workaround/fees do not save it); found no adequate historical analogue; expressly rejected the Second Circuit’s contrary approach in United States v. Vereen (circuit split).
Why it matters (factual): Binding in the Fifth Circuit (TX/LA/MS) that those core GCA interstate handgun-sale rules are unconstitutional. Nationwide effect and injunction scope still depend on remedy/mandate and any further review (rehearing / cert).
Primary opinion PDF: https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/opinions/pub/25/25-11206-CV0.pdf
FPC case summary (secondary): https://www.firearmspolicy.org/fifth-circuit-strikes-down-federal-interstate-handgun-purchase-ban

2) Fifth Circuit — United States v. Cordova, No. 24-50564
Watchlist had en banc grant Sep 14 2026 with argument TBD. CA5 en banc session page now lists Cordova for rehearing in the January 2027 en banc session (with USA v. Squire). Exact hearing date within that session not further specified on the page.
Why it matters (factual): Moves the en banc 922(g)(1) challenge from TBD to a scheduled session window.
Primary: https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/news/en-banc-session

Unchanged this pass (brief): No new SCOTUS order lists Sep 18–21; Johnson 26-255 & Novotny 25-1324 still DISTRIBUTED for Conf 9/28/2026; Viramontes/Grant still SET FOR ARGUMENT Dec 2 2026; no new FR firearms/ATF/DOJ/NFA publication today; AB 2047 still enrolled/at Governor; no verified new Hendrix/Silencer Shop DOJ appeal filing.

item.title: 2A alert: 5th Cir. strikes federal interstate handgun purchase ban (Elite Precision Customs v. ATF, 2–1, Sep 18)
item.description:
2A alert (~5:27 PM ET Fri Sep 18):

Elite Precision Customs v. ATF — Fifth Circuit strikes federal interstate handgun purchase ban.

What is new:
• U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit (No. 25-11206), opinion filed Sep. 18, 2026 (Doc. 83-1).
• Caption: Elite Precision Customs L.L.C.; Tim Herron; Freddie Blish; Firearms Policy Coalition, Inc. v. ATF; AG Todd Blanche; Acting ATF Director Daniel Driscoll.
• Panel: Judge Jerry Smith (author), Judge Engelhardt; Judge Haynes dissenting.
• Holding: the federal “Nonresident Handgun Purchase Ban” — 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(a)(3), 922(a)(5), and 922(b)(3) — is unconstitutional under the Second Amendment.
• Disposition: judgment of dismissal REVERSED; judgment RENDERED for the plaintiffs (appeal from N.D. Tex. No. 4:25-CV-44).

Why it matters:
Those provisions (together) bar direct interstate handgun sales (FFL to out-of-state buyer), with long-gun on-site interstate sales having statutory carve-outs. The court applied Bruen/Rahimi, cited Reese on purchase rights, rejected the Second Circuit’s Vereen approach (Ban upheld; cert denied), and found founding-era analogues inadequate.

Caveats:
• Binding in the Fifth Circuit — not a Supreme Court ruling and not automatically nationwide.
• 2–1 decision; government can seek rehearing en banc or certiorari (opinion silent on stay/mandate timing).
• Final ordered line does not quote “permanent injunction granted” or a nationwide ATF non-enforcement order.
• Court did not independently strike ATF’s parallel regulation 27 C.F.R. § 478.99(a); does not rewrite long-gun interstate rules or decide other § 922 provisions (e.g., age bans).
• SAF is not a party.

Sources:
• Opinion PDF: https://assets.nationbuilder.com/firearmspolicycoalition/pages/10076/attachments/original/1789762991/2026.09.18_083-1_OPINION.pdf?1789762991
• FPC announcement: https://www.firearmspolicy.org/fifth-circuit-strikes-down-federal-interstate-handgun-purchase-ban
• FPC case hub: https://www.firearmspolicy.org/eliteprecision

item.title: 2A alert: OLC says federal 18–20 handgun purchase ban (922(b)(1)/(c)(1)) unconstitutional as applied — dealers may not face criminal penalties
item.description:
2A alert — DOJ Office of Legal Counsel opinion (Sep 17, 2026):

Title: Application of 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) to Young Adults — Memorandum Opinion for the Attorney General.

What it says:
• OLC concludes §§ 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) are unconstitutional as applied to law-abiding young adults ages 18–20 who seek to purchase handguns from federally licensed dealers.
• Those adults are among “the people”; handguns are arms in common use; barring FFL handgun sales burdens the right to keep and bear arms under Bruen / Wolford.
• Government cannot show a Founding-era tradition that justifies the ban.
• Dealers may not be subjected to criminal penalties for selling handguns to that class.

Caveats (important):
• This is an OLC opinion advising DOJ on enforcement — not a court judgment striking the statute nationwide.
• Scope is handguns / FFL sales. Federal law already allows 18–20 purchases of rifles and shotguns from dealers.
• Does not by itself erase state 21+ handgun laws.

Why it matters:
DOJ’s own Office of Legal Counsel told the Attorney General the Gun Control Act’s 21-for-handguns rule fails Bruen/Wolford for 18–20-year-olds — a major enforcement-side development in the under-21 litigation lane (Reese / McCoy / NRA v. Bondi).

Primary: https://www.justice.gov/olc/media/1461811/dl

Factual briefing only — not advocacy. Flag NEW vs BACKGROUND.

================================================================================
MATERIAL / NEW
================================================================================

1) NEW (reported Thu Sep 17 evening ET): President Trump ordered DOJ not to appeal N.D. Tex. Judge James Wesley Hendrix’s permanent injunction limiting ATF enforcement of challenged National Firearms Act provisions covering short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and silencers/suppressors.

   Case: Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF (consolidated with Jensen v. ATF), No. 6:25-cv-00056-H (N.D. Tex.). Judgment/injunction entered Aug 5, 2026; stay expired and injunction took effect Aug 13 after DOJ did not seek emergency appellate relief.

   What CBS reported (sources familiar with the matter; not a published White House/DOJ press release):
   - The President decided against appealing and told some Republican members of Congress he would ensure DOJ did not contest the decision.
   - A DOJ official said the department intends to tell Congress it will not appeal.
   - ATF guidance to implement the court’s order is expected (CBS/WTX: “soon”).
   - Formal appeal deadline: October 5, 2026 — so the no-appeal posture is not yet procedurally final until that window closes (or a notice of appeal is filed).

   BACKGROUND / SCOPE (unchanged from Aug ruling; important caveats):
   - Injunction is party-/member-/customer-limited (plaintiff groups, current and future members/customers as applicable, plus certain joining state entities) — not a nationwide vacatur for all persons.
   - Machineguns and destructive devices were not the categories the court treated the same way under the zero-tax theory.
   - Other parties could still seek intervention/appeal; Congress could legislate.
